summary:
Session 2026-11-25 (pre-open, day before Thanksgiving). Context: 11-24 closed SPY -0.49% (718.8), QQQ -1.99% (638), XLK -3.3%, with defensives and consumer up (XLV +2.95%, XLP +1.7%, XLY +0.7%). Pre-market is worse: SPY -1.95% (705), QQQ -2.9% (620, the 11-20 low was ~596), VIXY +9%. Drivers are a WSJ report of sweeping new tariffs on China, the EU and 14 others (announcement possible this week) and AI-hardware multiple compression. PCE was due at 08:30 ET but was not yet in the feed. The Dec 9 Fed hike is ~96% priced.
Portfolio: only AS is open, 7% of equity (cost 30.53, close 30.14, -1.3%, +1.6% on a -2% QQQ day), stop 26.42, target 34.05, horizon 12-08. No company news; pre -1.7% is less than the tape. Held. Cash is 93%, so equity is about -2.1% against SPY about -8% since 10-29.
Examined, no trade: DELL (blowout beat and raise plus $25B buyback, but ISG margin guided down; -11.8% before the print, -5.6% pre, ~9x P/E; AI hardware beats are being sold, HPE -16%); HPQ (FY27 EPS guide in line, weak PCs, mixed); URBN (record Q3 but Anthropologie comps 1.7%, markdowns up, MS downgrade, -12% pre, priced); WDAY/ADSK/NTNX (-4.5%/-5%/-12% pre, priced); AMBA (-34% pre, priced); DE (EPS miss, pre -2.9% in line with the tape); ANT (Anthropic, below its $83 IPO price, $1T cap, no edge); SNY/INSM (priced M&A). The no-chasing rule is mixed: ANF closed +19.7% against pre-market +10.9%, while DKS faded to +14.6% and then flat.
Check next session (11-27 is an early close; 11-26 is closed, so the next session is the 11-27 pre-open): the PCE reaction and QQQ against ~596; tariff announcement details and AS exposure (Asia manufacturing); VIX below ~28; DKS/ANF drift; DELL/HPE for stabilisation; NVDA/Bessent; CRWD 12-01; AS stop 26.42. Redeploy only on stabilisation plus idiosyncratic catalysts, ideally on names that did not gap.
feedback: The economic_calendar tool still showed 08:30 ET releases (PCE, GDP) as "not out yet" about 3-5 minutes after the release time; a feed timestamp or "last updated" field would help. The digest's pre-market list is dominated by thin prints (<1% of average volume), so adding a minimum volume filter would make it more useful. Otherwise nothing blocked a trade this session.
